pages.headline: A new expert report changes the claim. The handler reopens years of records and asks what it means for the last approved position.
pages.body: A medical allegation needing a chronology. A disputed construction duty. A warranty breach tied to the deal record. A contamination event spanning policy years. A litigation update needing fresh authority. A recovery demand awaiting proof. Each requires facts, assumptions and a specialist decision. Orcaworks keeps the case current across claims systems, policy records, expert reports and correspondence.
pages.callout: Claims in our market are still a human business
pages.calloutSource: Colin Masson, Chief Claims Officer · Munich Re Specialty, 2025

pages.eyebrow: 01 / Medical professional liability · Allegation to reviewed position
pages.title: Medico-legal claim assessment
pages.problem: A new allegation or expert opinion raises a question about care, causation or liability. The handler reconstructs years of medical records, claim notes and correspondence, then checks which facts support or contradict the issue. Missing records and untested assumptions must be separated before the medico-legal specialist can decide the claim position.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks builds an issue-specific chronology, connects assertions to source evidence and identifies missing records or conflicting accounts. Medico-legal specialists, claims authorities and counsel determine causation, liability and coverage; the approved position and next evidence request remain linked to the case.

pages.eyebrow: 02 / Design liability · Project record to issue assessment
pages.title: Construction professional liability
pages.problem: A claim alleges a professional design or coordination failure after a project problem. The handler gathers appointments, drawings, RFIs, change instructions, site records and technical reports to establish who knew what and when. The record crosses firms and revisions, while technical experts and counsel still need a defensible account of the alleged failure.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks connects the alleged failure to the professional scope, project chronology and expert evidence, exposing revision conflicts and missing facts. Qualified technical reviewers and counsel assess duty, causation and coverage before the approved issue position and follow-up are retained.

pages.eyebrow: 03 / Transactional risk · Notice to defensible position
pages.title: R&W / W&I breach and loss assessment
pages.problem: A warranty claim arrives after completion of a deal. The handler reconstructs the sale agreement, disclosure letter, data-room snapshot, diligence and deal correspondence, then compares the alleged pre-close fact with the claimed post-close loss. Each warranty can require a different evidentiary path before counsel can assess breach, coverage and quantum.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks organizes the notice around the relevant warranty, disclosure evidence, chronology and loss assumptions. Claims specialists and counsel determine breach, causation, coverage and quantum; the approved position and precise requests for missing deal or financial evidence stay with the case.

pages.eyebrow: 04 / Environmental liability · Site history to current position
pages.title: Environmental long-tail assessment
pages.problem: New contamination evidence or a scientific report changes a claim spanning decades. The handler searches policy years, site ownership, operational history, remediation records and prior litigation to establish the relevant events and unresolved gaps. The environmental specialist and coverage counsel need a reliable sequence before addressing triggers, allocation and the next remediation decision.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks builds a source-linked site and policy chronology, separates facts from scientific assumptions and flags changes to the prior position. Environmental specialists, claims authorities and counsel decide coverage, allocation and remediation strategy before the authorized assessment and action are recorded.

pages.eyebrow: 05 / D&O / E&O · Material change to authorized response
pages.title: Professional-lines authority review
pages.problem: Counsel sends an updated report on a professional-lines claim. The handler compares pleadings, expert evidence, defense spend, reserves and the last approved authority to establish what has materially changed. The next committee or delegated approver needs a concise recommendation supported by the record before deciding a reserve, settlement or litigation response.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks compares new litigation evidence with the last approved position and prepares the authority pack with changes, uncertainties and sources. Counsel and the claims authority approve the response; rationale, authority limits and the next review checkpoint return to the claim.

pages.eyebrow: 06 / Recovery operations · Demand evidence to next response
pages.title: Subrogation and recovery follow-through
pages.problem: A recovery opportunity has been identified, but the demand lacks a payment record, liability exhibit or response from another carrier. The recovery specialist reopens the claim, checks correspondence and chases the missing proof. The recovery platform tracks the matter, yet someone still has to decide the next request, escalation or negotiation step.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks connects the recovery case, payments, liability evidence, demand package and response history. The specialist approves the next demand, negotiation or escalation; approved communications and the disposition are recorded, with unresolved external replies retaining an owner and review date.

pages.title: Keep the case current as the evidence changes
beforeItems: Medical, project, deal and policy evidence lives outside the claim record.
Handlers reconstruct the same history for each new issue or report.
Prior assumptions and authority can be hard to trace at the next review.
Evidence requests and approved decisions sit in separate correspondence.
afterItems: An issue-linked record connects facts, assumptions, gaps and supporting sources.
New material is assessed against the current approved position.
Qualified specialists and designated claims authorities retain each decision.
Approved rationale and the next owned action remain with the claim.
